import sys, json

# The MENU of this file space (GH #908): asked on `in_schemas` with the names a
# collector declares, it answers the declaration of every `file_*` tool it
# serves and names every other name in `unknown` -- the answer shape of
# `memory-hive/schemas` and the tools hive, byte for byte, so a collector merges
# it as one more answerer (`context.tool_answerer` 'files', stamped by the
# member). `*` asks for all 37, or all 40 where `projection_tools` is "1"
# (GH #980); the surfaces declare only the reads.
# --8<-- file-offer
# THE FILE TOOLS, one list, one entry per tool (GH #908). It stands WORD FOR
# WORD in `./schemas` (which hands it to a model's menu) and in `./tools` (which
# checks every call against it before a request leaves), because a code cell
# has no library it could share: `gh908_every_file_tool_maps_to_one_op.rs`
# holds the two copies to one value. The name IS the mapping: `file_<op>` asks
# the op `<op>`, `file_ws_<x>` the op `ws_<x>`; the one other rule is
# `PROJECTION_TOOLS` below, three names of the projection.
#
# Every description says the two things a model gets wrong without them: how a
# file is addressed, and that the `version` of an answer is the token a write
# has to pass back as `base` (a write against a moved head is merged or refused
# with `base_moved`, never applied blind). `raw`, `ws_tree` and the other
# projection ops (`ws_materialize`, `ws_adopt`, `ws_import_git`, `ws_pull`) are
# deliberately NOT here: bytes and the layout of a disk are no model's business.
# The folder tools of GH #947 follow the same rule: `file_dir_info` asks
# `dir_info`, `file_dir_summary` asks `dir_summary` (served by `./derive`),
# `file_create_dir` asks `create_dir`.
#
# GH #980: a writer that changes code runs its tests, exports and pushes with
# one call each -- `file_ws_exec` (`ws_exec` in a workspace it opened),
# `file_ws_export` (`ws_export_git` of the main line under a root; the git cell
# opens and discards the view itself) and `file_ws_push` (`ws_push` of that
# root's projection, to a remote the owner named). Before, a lab driver sent
# those ops in the model's place (gap L-2 of the coding proof). A menu names
# them only where the owner turned `projection_tools` on (`./schemas`).
ADDR = {"type": "string",
        "description": "the file: `fh-<12 hex>` or a path like `/notes/a.md`, "
                       "optionally with `@<version>`, `@ws:<name>` or `@snap:<name>`"}
WS = {"type": "string",
      "description": "the name of an open workspace to act in (optional)"}
BASE = {"type": "string",
        "description": "the `version` token of the answer this change was made against"}
FORCE = {"type": "boolean",
         "description": "skip the syntax hook (optional)"}
LINE = {"type": "integer", "description": "a 1-based line number"}
# GH #947: folders, the head of a file, one item of a file.
DIR = {"type": "string", "description": "a folder: an absolute path like `/notes`, `/` the root"}
HEAD_ADDR = {"type": "string",
             "description": "the file: `fh-<12 hex>` or a path like `/notes/a.md` (its current "
                            "version)"}
TO = {"type": "string", "description": "the new absolute path"}
NODE_ADDR = {"type": "string",
             "description": "one item of a file: `fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>` or `/notes/a.md#<anchor>`, "
                            "the anchor from `file_outline`"}
INSERT_ADDR = {"type": "string",
               "description": "the file: `fh-<12 hex>` or a path like `/notes/a.md`; ending in "
                              "`#<anchor>` (from `file_outline`) it names the item to insert at"}
CURSOR = {"type": "string", "description": "the `next` of the page before"}


def _obj(props, required):
    return {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required,
            "additionalProperties": False}


FILE_OFFER = [
    {"name": "file_info",
     "description": "Describe a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) -- path, kind, size, "
                    "summary line, snapshots -- and name its current `version`, the token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "ws": WS}, ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_read",
     "description": "Read lines `from`..`to` (1-based, negative counts from the end) of a "
                    "file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) or one `page` of a paged document "
                    "such as a PDF, each line as `<n>:<h4>|<text>`; on a file without pages "
                    "`page` 0 or 1 is ignored (named in `ignored`) and any other is "
                    "`page_unknown`, the answer's `version` is the token a write passes back "
                    "as `base`, and `more` names the next range when it was cut.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "from": LINE, "to": LINE,
                         "page": {"type": "integer",
                                  "description": "a page of a paged document, from 1; leave it "
                                                 "out for a file without pages"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_search",
     "description": "Search one file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) for a `pattern` -- "
                    "`exact`, `regex` or `semantic` -- and list the matching lines with their "
                    "`<n>:<h4>` marks and the `version` token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "pattern": {"type": "string", "description": "what to look for"},
                         "mode": {"type": "string", "enum": ["exact", "regex", "semantic"]},
                         "context": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 2,
                                     "description": "lines around each hit"},
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                                   "description": "the most hits"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file", "pattern"])},
    {"name": "file_summary",
     "description": "The summary of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), one line or "
                    "`short`, with the `version` token it describes -- the token a write "
                    "passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "level": {"type": "string", "enum": ["oneline", "short"]}},
                        ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_ask",
     "description": "Ask a question about one file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) and get "
                    "an answer with the line ranges it rests on and the `version` token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "question": {"type": "string", "description": "the question"}},
                        ["file", "question"])},
    {"name": "file_history",
     "description": "The history of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), newest first: "
                    "every move of its main line with op, time and version, and the current "
                    "`version` token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 200}},
                        ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_show",
     "description": "Show one version of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path): size, "
                    "author, parent and its first lines; its `version` is a token a write can "
                    "pass back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "version": {"type": "string", "description": "a version prefix"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_diff",
     "description": "The unified diff of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) between "
                    "version `a` and version `b` (or the current state), with the `version` "
                    "token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "a": {"type": "string", "description": "the older version"},
                         "b": {"type": "string", "description": "the newer version (optional)"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file", "a"])},
    {"name": "file_list",
     "description": "List the files and folders under a path `prefix`, each file with its "
                    "address `fh-<12 hex>`; reading one of them names the `version` token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"prefix": {"type": "string", "description": "a folder, `/` by default"},
                         "depth": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
                         "ws": WS}, [])},
    {"name": "file_find",
     "description": "Find files whose path matches a `glob` like `/notes/*.md`, each with its "
                    "address `fh-<12 hex>`; reading one of them names the `version` token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"glob": {"type": "string"},
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 500},
                         "ws": WS}, ["glob"])},
    {"name": "file_outline",
     "description": "The items of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path): classes, functions, "
                    "sections, keys or pages, each with its `anchor`, kind and line or page "
                    "span, read on with `fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>`; `next` is the `cursor` of the "
                    "next page, and the answer's `version` is the token a write passes back "
                    "as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "version": {"type": "string", "description": "a version prefix"},
                         "cursor": {"type": "string",
                                    "description": "the `next` of the page before"},
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 200}},
                        ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_links",
     "description": "The outgoing links of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) as written "
                    "in it -- imports, calls, links and URLs, each with the `anchor` it sits "
                    "in and its line; `next` is the `cursor` of the next page, and the "
                    "answer's `version` is the token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "version": {"type": "string", "description": "a version prefix"},
                         "cursor": {"type": "string",
                                    "description": "the `next` of the page before"},
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 200}},
                        ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_dir_info",
     "description": "One folder `path` page by page -- its counts, top topics and summary line, "
                    "then its subfolders and its files by path, each file with its address "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>` and the `version` token a write passes back as `base`; "
                    "`next` is the `cursor` of the next page.",
     "parameters": _obj({"path": DIR, "cursor": CURSOR,
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 200}},
                        ["path"])},
    {"name": "file_dir_summary",
     "description": "The one-line summary of a folder `path`, written anew from what lies in it "
                    "only when something under it changed; open a file in it by its address "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>` to get the `version` token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"path": DIR}, ["path"])},
    {"name": "file_create",
     "description": "Create a file at a new `path` from `text` (or `b64` bytes); the answer "
                    "names its address `fh-<12 hex>` and the `version` token the next write "
                    "passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"path": {"type": "string", "description": "an absolute path"},
                         "text": {"type": "string"},
                         "b64": {"type": "string", "description": "the bytes, base64"},
                         "mime": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["path"])},
    {"name": "file_replace",
     "description": "Replace the text `old` with `new` in a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a "
                    "path), exactly `expected` times (1 by default, or `all`), against the "
                    "`base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE,
                         "old": {"type": "string"}, "new": {"type": "string"},
                         "expected": {"type": ["integer", "string"],
                                      "description": "how many matches: a number or `all`"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "old", "new"])},
    {"name": "file_replace_regex",
     "description": "Replace every match of a regular expression `pattern` with `repl` in a "
                    "file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), `expected` times, against the "
                    "`base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE,
                         "pattern": {"type": "string"}, "repl": {"type": "string"},
                         "expected": {"type": ["integer", "string"],
                                      "description": "how many matches: a number or `all`"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "pattern", "repl"])},
    {"name": "file_replace_lines",
     "description": "Replace lines `from`..`to` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "with `new`, naming each old line's `h4` mark from the read in `hashes`, "
                    "against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "from": LINE, "to": LINE,
                         "hashes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
                         "new": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS},
                        ["file", "base", "from", "to", "hashes", "new"])},
    {"name": "file_insert",
     "description": "Insert `text` before or after `line` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or "
                    "a path), or before or after one item of it when the address ends in "
                    "`#<anchor>` (then without `line`), against the `base` token you read; the "
                    "answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": INSERT_ADDR, "base": BASE, "line": LINE,
                         "where": {"type": "string", "enum": ["before", "after"]},
                         "text": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "text"])},
    {"name": "file_delete",
     "description": "Delete lines `from`..`to` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` "
                    "token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "from": LINE, "to": LINE,
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "from", "to"])},
    {"name": "file_overwrite",
     "description": "Replace the whole content of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "with `text` (or `b64` bytes) against the `base` token you read; the "
                    "answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "text": {"type": "string"},
                         "b64": {"type": "string"}, "force": FORCE, "ws": WS},
                        ["file", "base"])},
    {"name": "file_patch",
     "description": "Apply a unified `diff` to a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` "
                    "token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "diff": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "diff"])},
    {"name": "file_snapshot",
     "description": "Give the current version of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) a "
                    "`name`, readable later as `@snap:<name>`; the answer names the `version` "
                    "token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "name": {"type": "string"}, "ws": WS},
                        ["file", "name"])},
    {"name": "file_revert",
     "description": "Make an earlier `version` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "its current one again, against the `base` token you read; the answer "
                    "carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE,
                         "version": {"type": "string", "description": "the version to restore"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "version"])},
    {"name": "file_remove",
     "description": "Remove a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) against the `base` token "
                    "(the `version` you read); its versions stay readable by address.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base"])},
    {"name": "file_create_dir",
     "description": "Create an empty folder `path` and the folders above it, so files can be "
                    "made there, each with its address `fh-<12 hex>` and its `version` token; "
                    "a folder that exists answers `created: false`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"path": DIR}, ["path"])},
    {"name": "file_remove_dir",
     "description": "Remove an empty folder `path` -- one that still holds a file or a folder "
                    "answers `not_empty` -- while every file elsewhere keeps its address "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>` and its `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"path": DIR}, ["path"])},
    {"name": "file_move",
     "description": "Move a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) to the new path `to`; it "
                    "keeps its address and its `version` token, the token its next write "
                    "passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": HEAD_ADDR, "to": TO}, ["file", "to"])},
    {"name": "file_copy",
     "description": "Copy a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) to the new path `to` as a "
                    "new file; the answer names the copy's address and its `version` token, "
                    "the token its next write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": HEAD_ADDR, "to": TO}, ["file", "to"])},
    {"name": "file_write_node",
     "description": "Replace the lines of one item of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>` "
                    "or a path with `#<anchor>`, the anchor from `file_outline`) with `text`, "
                    "against the `base` token you read, the current `version`; the answer "
                    "carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": NODE_ADDR, "text": {"type": "string"}, "base": BASE},
                        ["file", "text", "base"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_open",
     "description": "Open a workspace `name` over the files under `root`: pass its name as "
                    "`ws` to reads and writes (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path, `base` = the "
                    "`version` token you read) until it is committed or discarded.",
     "parameters": _obj({"name": {"type": "string",
                                  "description": "letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`"},
                         "root": {"type": "string", "description": "a folder, `/` by default"}},
                        ["name"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_status",
     "description": "The files a workspace `ws` touched, each with its address `fh-<12 hex>`, "
                    "state and its `base` and working `version` tokens.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_diff",
     "description": "The unified diff of everything a workspace `ws` changed against the "
                    "versions it started from (files by address `fh-<12 hex>`, each with its "
                    "`version` token).",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_patch",
     "description": "Apply a unified `diff` over several files (by path) inside a workspace "
                    "`ws`; the answer names every moved file's address `fh-<12 hex>` and new "
                    "`version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS, "diff": {"type": "string"}}, ["ws", "diff"])},

     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},

                    "gives `exit`, `out_tail` and `err_tail`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS,
                         "argv": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"},

                         "timeout_ms": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                                        "description": "a cap below the owner's (optional)"}},
                        ["ws", "argv"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_export",
     "description": "Export the main line under `root` (its files by address `fh-<12 hex>` at "

                    "logs it), or refuses `nothing_to_commit` when the tree is what the last "

     "parameters": _obj({"root": {"type": "string",
                                  "description": "the folder whose files are exported, like `/proj`"},

                        ["root", "note"])},

     "description": "Push the last export under `root` (the files by address `fh-<12 hex>` at "

                    "and `commit`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"root": {"type": "string",

# --8<-- end file-offer


doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
asked = (doc.get("body") or {}).get("tools")
if not isinstance(asked, list):
    # ABSENT and EMPTY are two requests: a caller that declared nothing gets
    # nothing, a request that lost its list is told so.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "schemas", "error_code": "tools_missing",
                   "schema_count": 0, "unknown_count": 0},
        "schemas": [], "unknown": [], "sidecar": [], "messages": []}))
    sys.exit(0)

# GH #980: the three projection tools are on the menu only where the owner
# turned them on -- the same override that gives the projection its
# `base_path`, one line more. Without a projection they would refuse every
# call (`no_base_path`), and no model should see a tool that always refuses.
P = doc.get("params") or {}
PROJECTION = ("file_ws_exec", "file_ws_export", "file_ws_push")
offered = str(P.get("projection_tools") or "0").strip() == "1"
served = [t["name"] for t in FILE_OFFER if offered or t["name"] not in PROJECTION]
names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)]
if "*" in names:
    wanted, unknown = list(served), []
else:
    seen, wanted, unknown = set(), [], []
    for n in names:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        (wanted if n in served else unknown).append(n)
by_name = {t["name"]: t for t in FILE_OFFER}
schemas = [{"name": n, "description": by_name[n]["description"],
            "parameters": by_name[n]["parameters"]} for n in wanted]
header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown,
                             "sidecar": [], "messages": []}))

description.purpose: The menu of this file space: asked with the tool names a collector declares, it answers `{name, description, parameters}` for every `file_*` tool it serves and names every other name in `unknown` -- the answer shape of `memory-hive/schemas`, so a collector merges it as one more answerer. `*` asks for all 37 tools: fourteen reads, sixteen writes, seven workspace ops -- and, where the owner set `projection_tools` to "1", the three projection tools `file_ws_exec`, `file_ws_export` and `file_ws_push` beside them (40, GH #980).
description.use_when: Reached on this hive's `in_schemas` lane, on an asking collector's menu tick. Never part of a tool round.
description.not_in_scope: No tool for `raw`, `ws_tree` or the projection ops other than `ws_exec`, `ws_export_git` and `ws_push`, and none of those three unless `projection_tools` is "1"; and no sidecar section: a file space asks a model for nothing in return. Which surface may write is not decided here but in `./tools`.
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: one declaration per asked name this space serves, in the order asked (`*` in menu order). unknown[]: the names it does not serve, verbatim; hop.error_code `tool_unknown` then, `tools_missing` when the request carried no `tools` list. sidecar[] is always empty.
description.consumes_meaning: A menu question: `tools`, the names the asking collector declares.
